it.key: Friction is a force that acts between two surfaces that touch each other, and it always acts against the direction of motion.
it.user:
Text: It slows down and stops because of friction. Friction is a force that acts between two surfaces that touch each other, and it always acts against the direction of motion. Even surfaces that look smooth have tiny bumps and hollows.
Key sentence: Friction is a force that acts between two surfaces that touch each other, and it always acts against the direction of motion.

A.q: Two smooth, flat metal surfaces are moving together. What happens to friction?
opts: It stays the same
It goes away
It increases
It decreases
A.ans: It stays the same

B.q: A car moves forward on a flat road. What happens to the friction force as it moves?
opts: It acts in the opposite direction to the motion
It acts at the end of the car
It acts to slow the car down as it moves
It acts only as the car turns
B.ans: It acts in the opposite direction to the motion

it.key: The harder the two surfaces are pressed together, the greater the friction.
it.user:
Text: A rough surface such as a brick floor has larger bumps, so it produces more friction than a polished marble floor. The harder the two surfaces are pressed together, the greater the friction. That is why a box full of books is harder to push than an empty one.
Key sentence: The harder the two surfaces are pressed together, the greater the friction.

A.q: What happens when you push two rough surfaces together?
opts: It becomes lighter
It becomes less slippery
It becomes more slippery
It becomes heavier
A.ans: It becomes more slippery

B.q: Two blocks of wood and stone are pressed together. Which one would have greater friction?
opts: Both the blocks, since they are the same
Both the blocks, as the surface is same
The stone block, as it is harder
The wood block, as it is rougher
B.ans: The stone block, as it is harder

it.key: Oil and grease are put between the moving parts of machines, and ball bearings are fitted in the wheels of cycles, because rolling causes much less friction than sliding.
it.user:
Text: Sometimes we want to reduce friction. Oil and grease are put between the moving parts of machines, and ball bearings are fitted in the wheels of cycles, because rolling causes much less friction than sliding. On the other hand, the treads on tyres and the grooves on the soles of sports shoes are designed to increase friction and give a better grip.
Key sentence: Oil and grease are put between the moving parts of machines, and ball bearings are fitted in the wheels of cycles, because rolling causes much less friction than sliding.

A.q: Why is a bicycle wheel not sliding but rolling?
opts: It has no balls at all
It has balls that reduce friction
It has balls that make friction higher
It has balls that make friction lower
A.ans: It has balls that reduce friction

B.q: A wheel of a bike rolls, and a ball is fixed in it. What happens to friction?
opts: It becomes zero, as there is no ball
It goes up, as the wheel rolls more
It stays the same, as sliding is less
It goes up, as rolling adds more
B.ans: It stays the same, as sliding is less

it.key: When the switch is on, the circuit is closed and the bulb glows.
it.user:
Text: A switch is used to open or close this path. When the switch is on, the circuit is closed and the bulb glows. When it is off, there is a gap in the path and the current stops.
Key sentence: When the switch is on, the circuit is closed and the bulb glows.

A.q: What happens to a bulb's glow when a switch is on?
opts: It is stopped off
It stays off
It glows on the same
It glows on the off
A.ans: It glows on the same

B.q: A bulb glows when a switch is closed. What happens when it is open?
opts: No light, and the bulb stays off
Light, and the bulb is closed
No light, and the bulb stops glazing
Light, and the bulb glows as a result
B.ans: No light, and the bulb stays off

it.key: When two or more cells are joined, the positive terminal of one cell must be connected to the negative terminal of the next.
it.user:
Text: In a circuit diagram, the longer line stands for the positive terminal. When two or more cells are joined, the positive terminal of one cell must be connected to the negative terminal of the next. This arrangement is called a battery.
Key sentence: When two or more cells are joined, the positive terminal of one cell must be connected to the negative terminal of the next.

A.q: A circuit has two cells. The positive terminal of one cell is connected to the negative terminal of the next. What is this arrangement?
opts: A battery
A circuit
A wire
A loop
A.ans: A battery

B.q: A battery has its positive terminal on the left and its negative terminal on the right. What happens if you connect two more cells?
opts: The positive terminal stays on the left and stays on the right
Only the negative terminal is connected to the positive
The positive terminal is always the same as before
Both positive terminals must connect to the negative ones
B.ans: Both positive terminals must connect to the negative ones

it.key: In our homes, lights and fans are not joined in series.
it.user:
Text: However, if one bulb in a series circuit fuses, the path is broken and all the other bulbs go off too. In our homes, lights and fans are not joined in series. They are joined in parallel, so that each one can be switched on or off without affecting the others.
Key sentence: In our homes, lights and fans are not joined in series.

A.q: Two fans are on the same wall. Does one fuse, the other go off?
opts: Yes, because they are joined in series
No, because they are joined in parallel
Yes, because they are joined in parallel
No, because they are joined in series
A.ans: No, because they are joined in parallel

B.q: Why do a fan and a bulb stay on together in a house?
opts: They are joined in series, so the fan is always on
They are joined in parallel, not series
They are joined in series, so the bulb turns off
They are joined in parallel, so one can be on
B.ans: They are joined in parallel, not series

it.key: In human beings, sound is produced by the voice box, called the larynx, at the upper end of the windpipe.
it.user:
Text: When the vibration stops, the sound also stops. In human beings, sound is produced by the voice box, called the larynx, at the upper end of the windpipe. Two vocal cords are stretched across it, and air from the lungs makes them vibrate.
Key sentence: In human beings, sound is produced by the voice box, called the larynx, at the upper end of the windpipe.

A.q: What organ produces sound in humans?
opts: lungs
throat
larynx
tongue
A.ans: larynx

B.q: A person has stopped breathing. What happens to their sound?
opts: It continues if the larynx remains open
It stops, as the windpipe is empty
It is louder because the windpipe is shorter
It is louder, as sound travels faster
B.ans: It stops, as the windpipe is empty

it.key: If you put your ear to one end of a long table and a friend taps the other end gently, you hear the tap clearly through the wood.
it.user:
Text: Sound travels faster in solids than in air. If you put your ear to one end of a long table and a friend taps the other end gently, you hear the tap clearly through the wood. The number of vibrations in one second is called the frequency, and it is measured in hertz.
Key sentence: If you put your ear to one end of a long table and a friend taps the other end gently, you hear the tap clearly through the wood.

it.key: The human ear can hear sounds with frequencies from about 20 hertz to 20,000 hertz.
it.user:
Text: A high frequency gives a high-pitched sound, like a whistle, while a low frequency gives a low-pitched sound, like a drum. The human ear can hear sounds with frequencies from about 20 hertz to 20,000 hertz. Sounds below this range are called infrasonic, and sounds above it are called ultrasonic.
Key sentence: The human ear can hear sounds with frequencies from about 20 hertz to 20,000 hertz.

A.q: A child hears a sound with a frequency of 3000 hertz. How is this sound heard?
opts: It is low-pitched, since it is above 20 hertz
It is high-pitched, since it is above 20 hertz
It is high-pitched, since it is below 20 hertz
It is low-pitched, since it is below 20 hertz
A.ans: It is high-pitched, since it is above 20 hertz

B.q: A child hears a sound with 20,000 hertz. What kind of sound does it belong to?
opts: Ultrasonic
Infrasonic
Low-pitched
High-pitched
B.ans: Ultrasonic

it.key: Imagine a line drawn at the point where the light hits the mirror, standing straight up from the surface at 90 degrees.
it.user:
Text: The ray of light that falls on the mirror is called the incident ray, and the ray that bounces back is called the reflected ray. Imagine a line drawn at the point where the light hits the mirror, standing straight up from the surface at 90 degrees. This line is called the normal.
Key sentence: Imagine a line drawn at the point where the light hits the mirror, standing straight up from the surface at 90 degrees.

A.q: What line drawn at the point where the light hits the mirror shows the light has just bounced back?
opts: The incident ray
The reflected ray
The reflected normal
The normal line
A.ans: The reflected ray

B.q: A ray of light hits a mirror at a 90-degree angle. What line is drawn at the point of contact?
opts: A line running from the mirror to the light
A line going back from the mirror
A line at the corner of the mirror
A line standing straight up from the mirror
B.ans: A line standing straight up from the mirror

it.key: The second law says that the incident ray, the normal and the reflected ray all lie in the same plane.
it.user:
Text: So if a ray strikes a mirror at an angle of incidence of 30 degrees, it will be reflected at 30 degrees. The second law says that the incident ray, the normal and the reflected ray all lie in the same plane. A plane mirror forms an image that is upright and of the same size as the object.
Key sentence: The second law says that the incident ray, the normal and the reflected ray all lie in the same plane.

A.q: A ray strikes a plane mirror at 30 degrees. What is the angle between the incident ray and the normal?
opts: 60 degrees
30 degrees
15 degrees
90 degrees
A.ans: 60 degrees

it.key: The image is also laterally inverted, which means that your left hand appears as the right hand of the image.
it.user:
Text: If you stand 2 metres in front of a mirror, your image seems to be 2 metres behind it, that is, 4 metres away from you. The image is also laterally inverted, which means that your left hand appears as the right hand of the image. This is why the word AMBULANCE is written in reverse on the front of ambulances.
Key sentence: The image is also laterally inverted, which means that your left hand appears as the right hand of the image.

A.q: A man is 2m in front of a mirror. What does his image look like?
opts: His image is behind him, 4m away
His image is behind him, 2m away
His image is behind him, 2m in front
His image is behind him, 4m in front
A.ans: His image is behind him, 4m in front

it.key: Every magnet has two poles, a north pole and a south pole.
it.user:
Text: Materials that are attracted by a magnet are called magnetic materials, while materials such as wood, plastic, rubber and glass are non-magnetic. Every magnet has two poles, a north pole and a south pole. The attraction is strongest near the poles.
Key sentence: Every magnet has two poles, a north pole and a south pole.

A.q: A magnet has two poles, a north pole and a south pole. What does it attract?
opts: Only the north pole
Both poles
Only the south pole
No poles
A.ans: Both poles

B.q: How many poles does a magnet have?
opts: Three
Two
One
Four
B.ans: Two

it.key: When two magnets are brought close, like poles repel each other and unlike poles attract each other.
it.user:
Text: This property is used in a compass, which travellers and sailors have used for centuries to find directions. When two magnets are brought close, like poles repel each other and unlike poles attract each other. Breaking a magnet does not separate its poles: each broken piece becomes a new magnet with its own north and south pole.
Key sentence: When two magnets are brought close, like poles repel each other and unlike poles attract each other.

A.q: Two compass needles are brought together. How do their poles attract each other?
opts: Like poles attract each other
All of them attract
No poles attract each other
Unlike poles attract each other
A.ans: Unlike poles attract each other

B.q: Two poles of a compass are brought closer. What happens?
opts: Like poles push each other away
Both poles become a new magnet
Like poles attract each other
Both poles turn to the south pole
B.ans: Like poles push each other away

it.key: Magnets lose their magnetism if they are heated, hammered or dropped often.
it.user:
Text: Breaking a magnet does not separate its poles: each broken piece becomes a new magnet with its own north and south pole. Magnets lose their magnetism if they are heated, hammered or dropped often. To keep them safe, bar magnets are stored in pairs with their unlike poles on the same side, separated by a piece of wood.
Key sentence: Magnets lose their magnetism if they are heated, hammered or dropped often.

A.q: How does a bar magnet lose its magnetism?
opts: It gets colder
It gets wetter
It gets heated
It gets heavier
A.ans: It gets heated

B.q: A magnet is hammered and then dropped. What happens?
opts: It loses its magnetism
It stays magnetized
It becomes a new magnet
It remains a magnet
B.ans: It loses its magnetism

it.key: Pressure is the force acting on a unit area of a surface.
it.user:
Text: Meena later learnt the reason in her science class. Pressure is the force acting on a unit area of a surface. When the same force acts on a smaller area, the pressure is greater.
Key sentence: Pressure is the force acting on a unit area of a surface.

A.q: Meena pushes a stone with a force. What happens to the pressure when the area of the stone is smaller?
opts: It becomes higher
It becomes lower
It stays the same
It becomes zero
A.ans: It becomes higher

B.q: A student pushes on a table harder than the same force on a bigger surface. What does this show?
opts: The bigger surface has more pressure
The bigger surface is not a surface at all
The bigger surface is smoother
The same force is acting on both
B.ans: The bigger surface has more pressure

it.key: Porters carrying heavy loads on their heads place a round piece of cloth under the load.
it.user:
Text: The same idea explains many things Meena had seen. Porters carrying heavy loads on their heads place a round piece of cloth under the load. The cloth increases the area of contact, so the pressure on the head is reduced and the load is easier to carry.
Key sentence: Porters carrying heavy loads on their heads place a round piece of cloth under the load.

A.q: What helps a porter carry heavy loads on their head?
opts: A piece of cloth under the load
A piece of cloth on the load
A piece of cloth on the head
A piece of cloth on the body
A.ans: A piece of cloth under the load

B.q: Meena lifts a heavy bag on her head. What happens to the pressure on her head?
opts: The cloth on the bag causes it to sink
The cloth on the bag adds more area
The cloth on the bag makes the bag bigger
The cloth on the bag is heavier than the bag
B.ans: The cloth on the bag adds more area

it.key: Water presses on the walls of its container, and the pressure increases with depth.
it.user:
Text: Liquids and gases also exert pressure. Water presses on the walls of its container, and the pressure increases with depth. That is why the walls of a dam are made much thicker at the bottom than at the top.
Key sentence: Water presses on the walls of its container, and the pressure increases with depth.

A.q: A dam has a narrow top and a wide bottom. How does the water pressure change?
opts: It increases with depth
It decreases with depth
It stays the same
It goes up and then down
A.ans: It increases with depth

B.q: A river flows through a dam. What happens to the water pressure as it flows deeper?
opts: It grows weaker as it rises up
It grows stronger and holds more pressure
It gets smaller, as the walls are thinner
It grows weaker because it is gas
B.ans: It grows stronger and holds more pressure

it.key: Tasting is not a safe way to test a substance, so we use indicators.
it.user:
Text: Substances that taste bitter and feel soapy, such as baking soda, are called bases. Tasting is not a safe way to test a substance, so we use indicators. An indicator changes its colour when it is added to an acid or a base.
Key sentence: Tasting is not a safe way to test a substance, so we use indicators.

A.q: How do we test a substance that is bitter?
opts: By tasting it
By smelling it
By putting it in water
By putting it in an acid
A.ans: By tasting it

B.q: A student uses a stick to taste a substance. What will happen to the stick?
opts: It will turn yellow
It will become green
It stays unmarked
It turns red, blue or green
B.ans: It turns red, blue or green

it.key: A turmeric stain on a white cloth turns red when soap, which is a base, is rubbed on it, and it turns yellow again when washed with plenty of water.
it.user:
Text: Turmeric is another natural indicator found in every Indian kitchen. A turmeric stain on a white cloth turns red when soap, which is a base, is rubbed on it, and it turns yellow again when washed with plenty of water. China rose petals give a solution that turns dark pink in an acid and green in a base.
Key sentence: A turmeric stain on a white cloth turns red when soap, which is a base, is rubbed on it, and it turns yellow again when washed with plenty of water.

A.q: A turmeric stain on a white cloth turns red when soap is rubbed. What will happen when it is washed with water?
opts: It will stay red, since soap is a base
It will turn yellow, since it is wet
It will stay red, since it is not wet
It will turn green, since it is wet
A.ans: It will turn green, since it is wet

B.q: A cloth with a turmeric stain gets rubbed with soap. What happens to the stain?
opts: It turns yellow, as it is already yellow
It turns red, as soap turns it
It stays red, as it is already red
It stays red, as soap is a base
B.ans: It turns red, as soap turns it

it.key: An ant bite injects formic acid into the skin, and the pain can be relieved by rubbing on a mild base such as moist baking soda.
it.user:
Text: Neutralisation is useful in daily life. An ant bite injects formic acid into the skin, and the pain can be relieved by rubbing on a mild base such as moist baking soda. Farmers add quicklime or slaked lime to soil that is too acidic.
Key sentence: An ant bite injects formic acid into the skin, and the pain can be relieved by rubbing on a mild base such as moist baking soda.

A.q: An ant bite causes pain. What should the person do to relieve it?
opts: Apply baking soda
Apply a mild soap
Apply antiseptic cream
Apply a cream with painkillers
A.ans: Apply baking soda

B.q: A farmer gets a sharp pain after a rainstorm. What should he do next?
opts: Rub moist baking soda on his skin
Put his skin under hot dry ice
Wash his skin with water and soap
Give him an antiseptic to kill bacteria
B.ans: Rub moist baking soda on his skin

it.key: When a sheet of paper is cut into pieces, each piece is still paper.
it.user:
Text: When ice melts into water, it is still water. When a sheet of paper is cut into pieces, each piece is still paper. Many physical changes can be reversed: water can be frozen back into ice.
Key sentence: When a sheet of paper is cut into pieces, each piece is still paper.

A.q: How many pieces of paper would there be if you cut a large sheet of paper into small pieces?
opts: One piece
Many pieces
Only one piece
Zero pieces
A.ans: Many pieces

B.q: A piece of paper is cut into two pieces. What is the piece's identity?
opts: It is still a piece of paper
It is now a sheet of paper
It is now water, after melting
It is a new type of paper
B.ans: It is still a piece of paper

it.key: Burning of wood, cooking of food, rusting of iron and the souring of milk into curd are all chemical changes.
it.user:
Text: When a piece of paper burns, it turns into ash, smoke and gases, and you cannot get the paper back. Burning of wood, cooking of food, rusting of iron and the souring of milk into curd are all chemical changes. A chemical change is often shown by signs such as the release of heat or light, a change in colour, the production of a gas, or a change in smell.
Key sentence: Burning of wood, cooking of food, rusting of iron and the souring of milk into curd are all chemical changes.

A.q: Which of the following shows a chemical change?
opts: A candle burns
A metal rusts
A cake is heated
A fruit is eaten
A.ans: A metal rusts

B.q: Why is rusting of iron a chemical change?
opts: It turns into iron oxide
It turns into carbon
It turns into iron in a gas
It becomes red and hot
B.ans: It turns into iron oxide

it.key: The wax vapour then burns in the flame to produce carbon dioxide, water vapour, heat and light, which is a chemical change.
it.user:
Text: When a candle burns, the wax first melts, which is a physical change. The wax vapour then burns in the flame to produce carbon dioxide, water vapour, heat and light, which is a chemical change. Crystallisation, in which pure crystals of a substance such as copper sulphate are obtained from its solution, is a physical change.
Key sentence: The wax vapour then burns in the flame to produce carbon dioxide, water vapour, heat and light, which is a chemical change.

A.q: A candle burns in the flame. What happens to its wax?
opts: It becomes lighter
It becomes a chemical
It turns to a gas
It turns to a liquid
A.ans: It becomes a chemical

B.q: What happens to a candle when it burns in a flame?
opts: The wax is cooled and the flame dies
The wax changes into a new substance
The wax melts, which is a physical change
A new substance is formed from the wax
B.ans: A new substance is formed from the wax

it.key: Sea water is let into shallow pits called salt pans and left there.
it.user:
Text: Along the coasts of Gujarat and Tamil Nadu, a lot of our common salt is obtained from sea water. Sea water is let into shallow pits called salt pans and left there. The heat of the sun slowly turns the water into vapour, a process called evaporation, and the salt is left behind as white crystals.
Key sentence: Sea water is let into shallow pits called salt pans and left there.

A.q: How is the salt obtained from sea water?
opts: It turns into vapor and stays behind
It turns into salt and stays in the pan
It turns into salt and is left in the pan
It turns into vapor and then gets dried
A.ans: It turns into vapor and stays behind

B.q: Why is salt obtained from sea water in these salt pans?
opts: The salt crystals turn back into salt
The salt is turned into salt crystals
The sun turns water into vapour
The salt is mixed with the salt pans
B.ans: The sun turns water into vapour

it.key: The clear water above can then be poured off gently into another vessel without disturbing the sand, which is called decantation.
it.user:
Text: This is called sedimentation. The clear water above can then be poured off gently into another vessel without disturbing the sand, which is called decantation. To remove the last fine particles, the water can be passed through filter paper.
Key sentence: The clear water above can then be poured off gently into another vessel without disturbing the sand, which is called decantation.

A.q: How can the sand be removed from the water?
opts: Pass it through a filter paper
Pour it gently into another vessel
Shake it in the vessel until all sand is gone
Pour it into a vessel where it is still clear
A.ans: Pour it gently into another vessel

B.q: A river has a clear water and sand above it. How is the sand removed?
opts: Pour the clear water into a new vessel
Pour the water into the river's mouth
Pour the water into a vessel to collect it
Pour the water through filters to clean it
B.ans: Pour the clear water into a new vessel

it.key: Stones are picked out of rice and dal by hand, which is called handpicking.
it.user:
Text: In villages, husk is separated from grain by winnowing, in which the mixture is dropped from a height in the wind, and the light husk is blown away while the heavier grain falls straight down. Stones are picked out of rice and dal by hand, which is called handpicking. Sieving is used in flour mills and at construction sites to separate fine particles from larger ones.
Key sentence: Stones are picked out of rice and dal by hand, which is called handpicking.

A.q: How do stones go to the mill from rice and dal?
opts: By hand, as they are light
By hand, as they are heavy
By machines, as they are light
By machines, as they are heavy
A.ans: By machines, as they are heavy

B.q: How is stone removed from rice and dal?
opts: By machine, as in winnowing
By water, as in washing
By hand, as in handpicking
By sieve, as in sievepicking
B.ans: By hand, as in handpicking

it.key: Aluminium foil used to wrap food and copper wires used in electrical fittings are made possible by these properties.
it.user:
Text: They are malleable, which means they can be beaten into thin sheets, and ductile, which means they can be drawn into wires. Aluminium foil used to wrap food and copper wires used in electrical fittings are made possible by these properties. Metals are good conductors of heat and electricity, which is why cooking vessels are made of metal and electric wires are made of copper.
Key sentence: Aluminium foil used to wrap food and copper wires used in electrical fittings are made possible by these properties.

A.q: Why can copper wires be used in electrical fittings?
opts: They are more brittle than copper
They are better at carrying heat
They are more ductile than copper
They are better at carrying electricity
A.ans: They are more ductile than copper

B.q: Why is copper used in wires?
opts: It is strong and tough
It is malleable and ductile
It is heavier than aluminium
It is good at carrying electricity
B.ans: It is good at carrying electricity

it.key: Solid non-metals are generally soft and dull, and they break into pieces when hammered.
it.user:
Text: Non-metals such as sulphur, carbon, oxygen and phosphorus behave very differently. Solid non-metals are generally soft and dull, and they break into pieces when hammered. They are poor conductors of heat and electricity.
Key sentence: Solid non-metals are generally soft and dull, and they break into pieces when hammered.

A.q: Why do solid non-metals break when hammered?
opts: They are very soft and break easily
They are very hard and do not break
They are very dull and do not break
They are very brittle and break easily
A.ans: They are very soft and break easily

B.q: A solid non-metal is hammered into a thin strip. What happens to it?
opts: It breaks into small pieces
It remains as a solid
It becomes a metal
It becomes a new solid
B.ans: It breaks into small pieces

it.key: Metals form oxides that are basic in nature, while non-metals form oxides that are acidic in nature.
it.user:
Text: Metals and non-metals also react differently with oxygen. Metals form oxides that are basic in nature, while non-metals form oxides that are acidic in nature. Sodium is so reactive that it is stored in kerosene.
Key sentence: Metals form oxides that are basic in nature, while non-metals form oxides that are acidic in nature.

A.q: A metal reacts with oxygen. What is the nature of the oxide?
opts: Basic
Acidic
Neutral
Neutral or acidic, depending on the metal
A.ans: Basic

B.q: Which metal forms a basic oxide?
opts: Copper, as copper forms acidic oxides
Mercury, as mercury always turns basic
Iron, as iron forms basic oxides
Oxygen, as it is an element that always turns basic
B.ans: Iron, as iron forms basic oxides

it.key: A substance that can burn is called a combustible substance or a fuel.
it.user:
Text: Combustion is a chemical process in which a substance reacts with oxygen to give off heat. A substance that can burn is called a combustible substance or a fuel. For combustion to happen, three things are needed together: a fuel, air to supply oxygen, and enough heat to raise the fuel to its ignition temperature.
Key sentence: A substance that can burn is called a combustible substance or a fuel.

A.q: A substance can burn but not ignite. What would it be called?
opts: a fossil fuel
a reactive fuel
a combustible substance
a non-fuel
A.ans: a combustible substance

B.q: A fuel is burned in a fire. What does it become?
opts: Carbon monoxide
Fuel
Oxygen
Combustible substance
B.ans: Combustible substance

it.key: Removing any one of these three things puts a fire out, and this is the idea behind every fire extinguisher.
it.user:
Text: Kerosene has a low ignition temperature, so it catches fire easily, while wood must be heated much more. Removing any one of these three things puts a fire out, and this is the idea behind every fire extinguisher. Water is the most common extinguisher.
Key sentence: Removing any one of these three things puts a fire out, and this is the idea behind every fire extinguisher.

A.q: How does a fire extinguisher work?
opts: It removes the fire's heat
It removes the fire's flame
It removes the fire's fuel
It removes the fire's ignition point
A.ans: It removes the fire's ignition point

B.q: A fire is spreading. Which one can stop it from spreading?
opts: The fire is stopped by burning
The fire is cooled
The fire is cut off
The fire is put out
B.ans: The fire is cut off

it.key: Being heavier than air, it forms a blanket around the fire, cutting off the supply of oxygen, and it does not harm electrical equipment.
it.user:
Text: For such fires, carbon dioxide is the best extinguisher. Being heavier than air, it forms a blanket around the fire, cutting off the supply of oxygen, and it does not harm electrical equipment. Covering a small fire with a blanket or sand works in the same way.
Key sentence: Being heavier than air, it forms a blanket around the fire, cutting off the supply of oxygen, and it does not harm electrical equipment.
